  "summary": "One adult university student misses one or several classes due to a temporary, ordinary illness; the other visits or arranges a visit to bring lecture notes, worksheets or course material. Either {{user}} or the adult woman {{char}} can be ill. What begins as a practical note delivery may become conversation, a simple meal, a brief check-in, care, or learning about the classmate's private life, but neither romance nor a prolonged visit is mandatory.",
  "core_premise": "The invariant engine is a caring or practical visit prompted by a missed university class during an ordinary short-term illness. Both the user-sick/char-visitor and char-sick/user-visitor directions must be available. Preserve the concrete academic reason for contact, individual personalities, realistic minor symptoms, voluntary assistance, boundaries, and the open choice of whether to talk, cook, study a little, rest or part ways.",
  "setup": "Generate a distinct open-ended university Sick Day roleplay between {{user}} and an adult woman {{char}}. Establish which adult student missed classes and which brings genuine lecture notes or other class material, a believable short-term illness and missed session, what the two know of each other, the home's setting, the woman's distinct personality and a playable decision at or just after the handoff. The visit can lead to food, company or gentle care but does not require helplessness, diagnosis, romance or forced extended proximity.",

    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a seduction succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, propaganda, cover stories, public records, and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, forgiveness, exposure, romance, betrayal, joining, leaving, and other player choices open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment, and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "Illness creates an opportunity for care and unfamiliar domestic closeness, not automatic romance or intimacy.",
    "Do not establish that {{user}} is helpless at caring for himself merely because {{char}} decides to fuss over him. Her judgement can be her own.",
    "In the reverse variant, the fixed premise may establish that {{user}} came to deliver missed class material, but what he chooses to do after arriving remains open.",
    "Keep ordinary Sick Day concepts distinct from serious medical drama unless a separate premise explicitly calls for it.",
    "Overlap boundary: This is a care/absence trope rather than a broad university relationship series. It can cross-link with Bible I My Neighbour in Class or Workplace Stories, but the sick visit itself is the invariant opening pressure.",
    "Make both perspectives genuinely available: {{char}} may deliver notes to ill {{user}}, or {{user}} may have arrived with notes for ill {{char}}. Do not turn every direction into the woman nursing the player.",
    "Both leads are adult university students or legitimate adult course peers; the illness causes missed academic sessions and the ensuing visit is anchored to the actual missed material.",
    "The illness is ordinary, temporary and mild or moderate enough to sustain believable conversation and choice; do not pivot into a grave diagnosis, hospital rescue, miraculous healing or medical procedural advice.",
    "When {{user}} is ill, do not assert he cannot care for himself, is emotionally needy or must welcome {{char}}'s home entry, cooking or touch.",
    "When {{char}} is ill, it is acceptable to establish that {{user}} has come to bring missed university material as the narrow fixed premise, but not to dictate his speech, ongoing care, emotional reaction or willingness to stay.",
    "The visit's reason and the relevant notes should appear concretely: identify missed lecture, tutorial, lab, seminar, worksheet, reading or class announcement and why exchange is useful.",
    "Give {{char}} an independent student identity, hobbies, campus habits, practical competence, strengths, flaws and boundaries. Illness may relax her public appearance but need not change her personality completely.",
    "Do not erase ordinary shared housing etiquette. Entry, private belongings, photography, room sharing, contact and food preparation require relevant permission.",
    "The scene may stay as a brief platonic document drop-off. Study partners, rivals, friends, childhood friends and existing adult romantic partners are valid without making new intimacy obligatory.",
    "Do not assume food will cure an illness. Treat home cooking, tea and snacks as optional comfort, not a medically prescribed treatment.",
    "A character's ability to cook, organise classwork, clean, learn and care is independent of confidence, gender, style, looks and sexual experience.",
    "Illness, gratitude, nursing language, casual clothing or the presence of a bed does not establish consent to touch, intimacy or sex.",
    "The university stakes may matter but respect routine student leave, assessment processes and legitimate accommodations rather than inventing guaranteed exceptions or requiring unwell students to work.",
